newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB makes foray into shipping for wheat sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB makes foray into shipping for wheat sales.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) will control shipping costs for at least 20 percent of the wheat it exports in 1997 and aims to increase its involvement in the freight market over time, the board said on Friday.
Greater control of the shipping would produce new long-term grain business, Michael Watson, recently-appointed head of AWB's sea freight business, said in a statement.
Most grain business was presently done on a free on board (fob) basis, he said.
"That really puts the control in the hands of the buyer. When we do business on a cost and freight basis (c and f) we have the control," he said.
It gave the AWB the ability to pick ships and the owners, control the quality and schedule of the ships and the opportunity to build relationships with ship owners, he said.
AWB arranged the shipping on a recent sale to a new mill in Sudan and the speed of making the first delivery weighed heavily in the AWB's favour in negotiating repeat business, he said.
"The owners give every indication that they now intend to form a long-term business relationship with the AWB," he said.
While most of the AWB's traditional customers were likely to continue to do business on a fob basis, recent business to government buyers in Egypt was on a c and f basis, he said.
"Others are expected to at least test our ability to compete with the service provided by their national lines," he said.
Last year, AWB chartered the 69,000 tonne MV Arthur Stove to carry five grades of wheat to six individual customers in Thailand, an emerging success story for the AWB, he said.
First shipments to Thailand of about 100,000 tonnes in 1994/95 had risen to nearly 250,000 tonnes last year. The market was expected to grow again this year, Watson said.
